quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark than in daylight. During the day, shadows and light help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lights distort these visual cues or make them disappear.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane lets the driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent side mirrors from working.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This makes you more visible in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger.
Are required for the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Both the driver and passenger must have footrests. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. This prevents your passenger from falling off and taking you with them.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:
questions.explanation: Wind noise can permanently damage your hearing if you are exposed to it for long periods. Wear ear protection when you ride. It will protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and horns.

questions.question: If you must ride on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid making sudden movements. Use both brakes gently when braking.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
Wear comfortable clothes like shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Wear bright colors when riding, even during the day. This makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, make sure it:

options.text: Fits loosely and flaps in the wind.
Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Is not made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. They should fit snugly enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself in your lane to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt before you continue riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. When you see one, you must come to a complete stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When being followed too closely by another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle someone following too closely is to let them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly to the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing while riding at any time of day.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Your boots or shoes should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as they are on your motorcycle.
Immediately take it out on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different in some ways. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Ride it in a controlled area first to get used to it before taking it on the road.
